claims.text: The new predictive approach incorporates atomic-scale defects.
The new predictive approach incorporates temperature-dependent interactions.
The new approach will estimate the thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than existing models.
The accuracy advantage will be particularly pronounced below 200 K.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is defect-free.
Atomic-scale defects interact with phonons and electrons in HfNbTaTiZr.
Defect-induced changes in phonon scattering change thermal conductivity.
Traditional models do not capture defect-induced changes in phonon scattering.
Existing models assume perfect crystals and do not account for defects.
At low temperatures, the new approach will predict thermal-conductivity values at least 20% higher than existing models predict.
Electronic contributions dominate thermal conductivity at high temperatures.
The magnitude of the prediction improvement depends on defect type and concentration.
The approach is applicable only below 200 K and is not intended for high-temperature scenarios.

contradictions.description: The initial alloy is declared defect-free, but defects are then treated as the structural mediator and the experiment uses samples with controlled defect densities. Applying a predictive method does not itself introduce defects, so the modeled and stated initial sample states are inconsistent.
The boundary restricts applicability to temperatures below 200 K, while the stated range and falsification measurements include 200 K.
